questions.passage: Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. A student in the front row is <u>ⓐ texting</u> on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are <u>ⓑ laughing</u> over something they are holding under their desks. Another student seems <u>ⓒ to be working</u> on her homework. Finally, here is a student who seems ready <u>ⓓ listening</u>. He has a supportive look on his face; he is actually <u>ⓔ waiting</u> for you to give your presentation.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] a student who seems ready to listen. [해석] 경청할 준비가 된 것처럼 보이는 학생이 있다. ready 뒤에는 to부정사가 온다.
det.correct: ⓐ is texting: 진행형 ✅ ⓑ are laughing: 진행형 ✅ ⓒ seems to be working: seem + to V ✅ ⓓ ready listening → ready to listen: ready 뒤에 to부정사 ❌ ⓔ is waiting: 진행형 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 ready + to V: be ready to listen(경청할 준비가 된). ready 뒤에 동명사(-ing) 불가. seem + to V: ~인 것처럼 보이다.

questions.passage: "The assignment is to write a speech about someone who you admire. It could be a historical figure, a celebrity, or even someone you personally know in your life," Ms. Harper told the class. My classmates began (A) [brainstorming / to brainstorm] a list of people they might pick. A few days later, Ms. Harper talked about how (B) [delivering / to deliver] a good speech. This reminded me that it wasn't just a writing assignment, but a speech I would have to give in front of my classmates! I'm (C) [too / so] shy to raise my hand in class even when I know the answer.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에서 어법에 맞는 표현을 골라 바르게 짝지은 것은?

det.ref: [원문] began brainstorming / how to deliver / too shy to raise
det.correct: (A) brainstorming: begin + Ving/to V 둘 다 가능하지만 원문은 brainstorming ✅ (B) to deliver: how + to V 구조 ✅ (C) too: too ~ to V (너무 ~해서 ...할 수 없다) ✅
det.tip: 🔑 (A) begin + Ving/to V 모두 가능 (B) 의문사 + to V: how to deliver (C) too ~ to V ≠ so ~ that: "I'm too shy to raise" = 너무 수줍어서 들 수 없다

questions.passage: My heart was racing so fast that I thought it might fly out of my chest. I could feel my face turning red. I blanked out.
questions.stem:
다음 중 밑줄 친 부분과 같은 구문 구조를 가진 것은?
My heart was racing so fast that I thought it might fly out of my chest.

det.ref: [원문] so ~ that 구문: so + 부사/형용사 + that + S + V
det.correct: 원문은 so + 부사(fast) + that + S + V 구조. ②도 동일한 so fast that 구조 ✅
wrongs: ① so ~ as to: 다른 구문
det.tip: 🔑 so ~ that: 너무 ~해서 ...하다 (결과). "I felt so proud of myself that I barely noticed how loudly everyone was clapping for me!" 도 같은 구문.

ch: She is so kind as to help everyone.
He ran so fast that he won the race.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication (A) [climate / weather]. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. When you discuss or (B) [evaluate / evacuate] others' speeches, be (C) [constructive / destructive] and helpful.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.ref: [원문] communication climate / evaluate / constructive
det.correct: (A) climate = 분위기 (weather = 날씨) (B) evaluate = 평가하다 (evacuate = 대피하다) (C) constructive = 건설적인 (destructive = 파괴적인) ✅
det.tip: 🔑 climate: 기후뿐 아니라 "분위기, 풍토"의 의미. evaluate ↔ evacuate 철자 혼동 주의. constructive ↔ destructive 반의어.

questions.passage: The big day for the speech finally arrived. I had spent the previous week ① <u>imagining</u> how my classmates would react to my speech. I was still mostly thinking about what my classmates might think. I wasn't putting much thought into what I was actually going to say. I ② <u>figured</u> I could just speak off the top of my head. I was sweating as I walked up to the front. My heart was racing so fast. I could feel my face turning red. I ③ <u>relaxed</u>. I just stood there silently.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~③ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.ref: [원문] I blanked out. I just stood there silently. → relaxed는 문맥과 반대.
det.correct: ③ relaxed(편안해졌다) → blanked out(머리가 하얘졌다). 땀, 빠른 심장박동, 빨간 얼굴 → 극도의 긴장 상태이므로 relaxed는 부적절 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 blank out = 머리가 하얘지다 (긴장으로 아무 생각이 나지 않음). relaxed(편안해진)는 반대 의미. figure = 생각하다, 판단하다.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will appreciate when others comment on your speech. Listening well is as important as speaking well.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] Good listeners can help speakers / Listening well is as important as speaking well.
det.correct: 글 전체가 좋은 청취자의 역할과 경청의 중요성을 설명하고 있다. ② 정답 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 주제 파악: 반복 키워드(listener, listen, listening)와 마지막 문장(Listening well is as important as speaking well)이 핵심.

ch: how to write a good speech
the importance of being a good listener
the role of teachers in speech education

questions.passage: "The assignment is to write a speech about someone who you admire." My classmates began brainstorming a list of people they might pick — mostly athletes, singers, and actors. However, I knew right away who my speech was going to be about. Grandma is the person I admire the most. Writing a speech about her would be a piece of cake.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.ref: [원문] I knew right away who my speech was going to be about. Grandma is the person I admire the most.
det.correct: Logan은 바로 할머니에 대해 쓰기로 결정했다. ③ 정답 ✅
wrongs: ④ a piece of cake(쉬운 일) ❌
det.tip: 🔑 a piece of cake = 매우 쉬운 일. right away = 즉시. admire = 존경하다.

ch: Logan did not know who to write about.
Most classmates chose to write about teachers.
Logan decided to write about his grandmother.
Writing the speech was very difficult for Logan.
The assignment was to write an essay.

questions.passage: I didn't want to drop the ball like the first time. So this time, I practiced delivering the speech. I stood in front of the mirror every day for a week and went over all the things I wanted to say. I used cue cards which contained key phrases about important facts. I rehearsed how I would stand, how I would make eye contact with the audience, and even when I would pause.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.ref: [원문] I used cue cards which contained key phrases. (핵심 문구가 담긴 큐카드를 사용)
det.correct: ④ 전체 연설을 단어 하나하나 외웠다 → cue cards(핵심 문구 카드)를 사용했으므로 일치하지 않음 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 cue cards = 핵심 내용만 적은 메모 카드 ≠ 전체 암기. drop the ball = 실수하다. go over = 복습하다.

ch: Logan practiced in front of a mirror.
Logan used cue cards with key phrases.
Logan memorized the entire speech word by word.

questions.passage: "I was afraid the other students would laugh at me if my speech wasn't good enough." She replied, "You certainly can't control what others think about your speech. That means you should be focusing on the one thing you can control — _______________."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] the one thing you can control — how you give your speech.
det.correct: 통제할 수 없는 것(남의 생각)과 대비하여 통제할 수 있는 것(자신의 발표 방법)이 빈칸에 들어감. ③ 정답 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 빈칸 전략: can't control(통제 불가) ↔ can control(통제 가능)의 대비 구조. 핵심 교훈: 자신의 수행(performance)에 집중하라.

ch: what your classmates think about you
how many people are in the audience
whether the topic is interesting enough

questions.passage: "It's quite all right to fall short of your own expectations as long as you learn something from it," she said in a warm voice. "What was bothering you the most while you prepared for the speech?" "I was afraid the other students would laugh at me."
questions.stem:
밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
fall short of your own expectations

det.ref: [원문] fall short of your own expectations = 자신의 기대에 미치지 못하다
det.correct: fall short of = ~에 미치지 못하다, 부족하다. 선생님이 "실패해도 배우면 괜찮다"고 위로하는 맥락. ② 정답 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 fall short of = ~에 못 미치다 ↔ live up to = ~에 부응하다. as long as = ~하는 한.

questions.passage: I felt nervous again when the big day finally arrived. But when the teacher called my name, I noticed that my nerves had actually calmed down a bit. I felt way better than the last time, for sure! I walked up to the front of the class and looked out into the audience. My heart began to race, and I took a deep breath to calm it down.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용이 사실이면 T, 그렇지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"두 번째 발표 때 Logan은 첫 번째보다 덜 긴장했고, 심호흡으로 마음을 가라앉혔다."

det.ref: [원문] my nerves had actually calmed down a bit / I felt way better than the last time / I took a deep breath to calm it down.
det.correct: T: 첫 번째보다 나았고(felt way better), 심호흡을 했다(took a deep breath) → 제시문과 일치 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 calmed down = 진정되다. way better = 훨씬 나은. take a deep breath = 심호흡하다.

questions.passage:
The next day, I met Ms. Harper after school to talk about the speech.

(A) "What was bothering you the most while you prepared for the speech?"
(B) I said, "I'm embarrassed about the speech. I must have looked like a fool. I know I could have done better."
(C) "It's quite all right to fall short of your own expectations as long as you learn something from it," she said in a warm voice.
questions.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] 순서: Logan이 먼저 자신의 창피함을 말함(B) → 선생님이 위로(C) → 선생님이 추가 질문(A)
det.correct: (B) Logan 고백 → (C) 선생님 위로 → (A) 선생님 추가 질문: 자연스러운 대화 흐름 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 순서배열: 대화 흐름 파악. 학생 고백 → 선생님 위로 → 추가 질문. must have p.p. = ~했음에 틀림없다 (과거 추측).

questions.stem:
다음 중 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
I really should [have focused / focused] on my performance.

det.ref: [원문] I really should have focused on my performance. [해석] 나는 정말로 나의 수행에 집중했어야 했다.
det.correct: should have p.p. = ~했어야 했다 (과거에 하지 않은 일에 대한 후회). should have focused ✅
wrongs: ② focused: should 뒤에 have + p.p. 구조 필요 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 should have p.p.: 과거 후회 표현. "I should have studied harder." = 더 열심히 공부했어야 했다. should + V(원형): 현재/미래 의무.

questions.passage: Ms. Harper tried to help me out. "Start by telling us a bit about your grandmother, Logan." I spoke about what kind of work my grandmother used to do, but I quickly ran out of words to say. Then <u>she</u> said, "How about telling us a bit about why you admire her so much?"
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>she</u>가 가리키는 것은?

det.ref: [원문] Ms. Harper tried to help me out. ... Then she said, "How about telling us..."
det.correct: she는 Logan을 도와주려는 Ms. Harper를 가리킨다. 대화 문맥에서 질문하는 주체 = 선생님 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 지칭추론: 대화에서 she → 직전에 언급된 여성 인물(Ms. Harper). run out of = ~이 바닥나다.

questions.stem:
다음 중 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
I used cue cards [which / what] contained key phrases about important facts.

det.ref: [원문] cue cards which contained key phrases about important facts.
det.correct: which는 관계대명사로 선행사 cue cards를 수식. which contained = 포함하고 있는 ✅
wrongs: ② what: 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사이므로 앞에 cue cards가 있으면 사용 불가 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 which vs what: 선행사가 있으면 which/that, 선행사를 포함하면 what. cue cards which = the cue cards that.

questions.passage: I didn't want to drop the ball like the first time. ① So this time, I practiced delivering the speech. ② I stood in front of the mirror every day for a week and went over all the things I wanted to say. ③ The school cafeteria recently introduced a new menu featuring organic vegetables. ④ I used cue cards which contained key phrases about important facts. ⑤ I rehearsed how I would stand, how I would make eye contact with the audience, and even when I would pause.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?

det.ref: ③ 학교 급식실의 새 메뉴 → 연설 준비와 무관한 내용.
det.correct: ① 연습 결심 ✅ ② 거울 앞 연습 ✅ ③ 급식 메뉴 → 무관 ❌ ④ 큐카드 사용 ✅ ⑤ 리허설 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 무관문장: 글의 소재(연설 준비)에서 벗어나는 문장 찾기. drop the ball = 실수하다. go over = 복습하다.

questions.passage: Listening well is as ________ as speaking well.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 단어를 쓰시오. (1단어, i로 시작, 9자)

det.ref: [원문] Listening well is as important as speaking well.
det.correct: as ~ as 원급비교 구조에서 important(중요한)가 들어간다. "경청은 말하기만큼 중요하다" ✅
det.tip: 🔑 as + 형용사/부사 원급 + as: ~만큼 ...한. Listening well is as important as speaking well = 잘 듣는 것은 잘 말하는 것만큼 중요하다.

questions.passage: I felt so proud of myself that I barely noticed how loudly everyone was clapping for me!
questions.stem:
다음 조건에 맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.

[조건] 주어진 단어를 모두 사용, 필요시 어형 변환, 5단어로 작성
[보기] focus / on / should / my / have

[문장] I really ______________________ performance.

det.ref: [원문] I really should have focused on my performance.
det.correct: should have focused on my: should have p.p.(과거 후회) + focus on(~에 집중하다) + my(소유격) ✅
det.tip: 🔑 should have p.p. = ~했어야 했다. focus on = ~에 집중하다. 어순: should have focused on my performance.

questions.passage: That woke me up from the depths of despair. Of course, that was it! I wouldn't have been able to make my classmates like what I wanted to say. I really should have focused on my performance. A couple of weeks later, the class was given another speech assignment. I didn't want to _____________ like the first time.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] I didn't want to drop the ball like the first time.
det.correct: drop the ball = 실수하다, 기회를 놓치다. 첫 번째 발표에서 실패한 것처럼 다시 실수하고 싶지 않다는 의미. ② 정답 ✅
wrongs: ① make a speech: 연설하는 것 자체를 원하지 않는 게 아님 ❌
③ raise my hand: 손을 드는 것과 무관 ❌
④ blank out: 가능하지만 원문은 drop the ball ❌
⑤ give up: 포기가 아닌 실수 방지 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 drop the ball: 스포츠에서 유래한 관용어 = 실수하다, 맡은 일을 망치다. wake up from despair = 절망에서 깨어나다.

questions.passage: "You certainly can't control what others think about your speech. That means you should be focusing on the one thing you can control — how you give your speech." That woke me up. I really should have focused on my performance. So this time, I practiced delivering the speech. While my voice trembled from time to time, I managed to get my whole message across. When I was done, I felt so proud of myself that I barely noticed how loudly everyone was clapping for me!
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 Logan이 얻은 교훈으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] focusing on the one thing you can control — how you give your speech.
det.correct: 핵심 교훈: 남의 반응이 아니라 자신이 통제할 수 있는 것(자신의 수행)에 집중하라. ② 정답 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 글의 교훈/시사점: 반복되는 핵심 메시지(control, focus, performance)를 찾기. manage to V = ~하는 데 성공하다.

ch: You should always speak loudly to impress the audience.
Focus on what you can control — your own performance.
Avoid giving speeches if you are shy.
The most important thing is to make others laugh.
Practice is unnecessary if you know the topic well.
